To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the human growth hormone (hGH) receptor (hGhR) gene has a complex first exon region containing multiple promoters; (2) the highest expressing exon, V1, has a 1.5-kb 5'-flanking region; (3) this promoter is repressed; (4) six HNF-4 binding sites are present; and (5) these sites are functional in vitro.
HNF- 4alpha is developmentallly regulated in human liver, and HNF- 2alpha and HNF-8alpha are expressed in fetal liver, whereas only HNF-2alpha is present in adult liver.
the human growth hormone (GH) receptor gene has two modules of first exons, one of which is liver-specific and the other is ubiquitously expressed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the expression of the hGHR, a key component of the GH receptor complex that plays an important role in growth and development.
identifying the elements that regulate hGHR expression.
identifying the molecular basis of the developmental and tissue-specific expression of the hGHR gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the V1 exon hGHR promoter is repressed by multiple negative elements and activated by HNF- 4alpha2 and alpha8 in a dual manner.

the expression of the V1 hGhR gene is regulated by HNF-1alpha and HNF-1beta, which are expressed throughout development, and HNF- 4alpha2 and 4alpha8, which are expressed in the postnatal liver, thus providing a mechanism for the developmental and tissue-specific expression of the Vl hGhR mRNA in the human liver.
V1 hGhr gene expression is developmentally regulated and is controlled by the HNF-4 family of transcription factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HNF-1alpha and HNF-1beta are the major regulators of module B hGH gene expression in the liver, whereas HNF-4 is the primary factor regulating the V1 hGH receptor gene.
HNF-1alpha, HNF-4, and HNF-6 are the key transcription factors for hGHR gene regulation.
HNF- 4alpha2 and 4alpha8 are important for the developmental regulation of the human GH receptor gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is more than one HNF-4 isoform that is expressed in human fetal liver and that HNF4-alpha2 and HNF4-alpha8 are expressed in human fetal hepatocytes.
the V1 hGhr gene is repressed in tissues other than liver, but that HNF- 4alpha2 and/or HNF- 8alpha are able to activate the gene in liver.
HNF-1alpha, HNF-4, and GATA4 are the main factors regulating hGHR expression, but that HNF-6 is a key factor in the regulation of the module B promoters.
